title: Best Hospitality Operations Platforms in 2026
summary: Conduit, hotelkit, Flexkeeping, Quore, ALICE and Breezeway compared on guest tasks, maintenance, PMS write-back and published pricing.
body_markdown:
For guest tasks and maintenance in 2026, the platforms worth shortlisting are Conduit, hotelkit, Flexkeeping, Quore, ALICE by Actabl and Breezeway. Conduit publishes its rates, at $18 to $48 per unit per month. The other five quote on request, so budgeting starts with a sales call.


## How did we rank these platforms?


Ranking here turns on how much of the guest-to-task loop each platform closes without a person in the middle. A guest asks for a late checkout at 11pm. Something has to read the message, decide whether the request is allowed, create the task, route it to whoever is on shift, and tell the guest what happened. Most tools in this category start at step three, after a human has already typed the task in. Platforms that start at step one rank higher. Housekeeping depth, preventive maintenance and inventory still count, and the ops-first tools are stronger there, so those strengths are called out per vendor rather than averaged away.


## Which platform closes the guest-to-task loop without a person?


Conduit runs the guest message and the resulting task on the same agent, which is what separates it from the five ops-first tools below. Its Messaging package at $18 per unit per month carries inbound and outbound voice AI, a unified inbox, and PMS and OTA integrations, and the Full Suite package at $48 adds Tasks and Workforce, scheduling and dispatch, and inventory management. That matters because the handoff between "guest asked" and "someone did it" is where most operations software begins rather than ends. Conduit reports a 70 to 90 percent automation range across its base. Cash Flow Street, a 35-property manager, runs at 96 percent automation, up from 80 percent at launch, and Haven Vacation Rentals runs at 90 percent.


The watch-out is scope. Conduit is a guest communication platform that grew operations features, so a 400-room resort with a mature engineering department will find Quore and hotelkit deeper on preventive maintenance schedules and asset registers.


## Which platform is strongest on housekeeping and maintenance depth?


hotelkit and Flexkeeping are the two built around the back of house first, and both show it in the maintenance feature set. hotelkit covers tasks and communication, housekeeping, maintenance and internal communication, and describes automating maintenance cycles with consumption data, inventory and repairs recorded centrally ([hotelkit](https://www.hotelkit.net/en/) ). Flexkeeping covers housekeeping, maintenance, collaboration, task management and guest requests, and publishes two customer results: 13,778 tasks automated in three months, and a 716 percent return on investment ([Flexkeeping](https://www.flexkeeping.com/) ). Neither publishes pricing.


Both integrate with the PMS layer a hotel group actually runs. hotelkit lists Mews, Oracle Hospitality (OHIP/OPERA), apaleo and Stay. Flexkeeping lists Mews, Cloudbeds, Oracle Opera Cloud, RMS, Apaleo and Shiji.


## Which platform has the widest hotel-chain footprint?


Quore has the widest hotel-chain footprint of any platform in this group, with more than 120,000 users across major hotel brands ([Quore](https://www.quore.com/) ). It calls itself the Hospitality Orchestration Platform. Coverage spans housekeeping, work orders, guest requests and engineering, including preventive maintenance and asset management. Franchisees operating under a brand standard that already names Quore have usually had the integration question answered for them, which shortens the evaluation to whether the guest-messaging side is good enough.


Quore's own site does not mention AI capabilities, and it does not publish pricing or a specific PMS integration list. For an operator whose main problem is guest message volume rather than work-order tracking, that gap is the reason to look elsewhere.


## What does ALICE by Actabl cover?


ALICE is positioned as an all-in-one hotel operations platform spanning enterprise service delivery, housekeeping, messaging and guest services ([Actabl](https://actabl.com/alice/) ). Its four published areas are housekeeping, service delivery, guest services and guest messaging, which makes it the closest of the ops-first tools to covering the guest conversation as well as the task. Actabl also markets an Actabl AI product, though the ALICE page gives no detail on what that does inside ALICE.


Pricing is not published, and the ALICE page does not list its PMS integrations. ProfitSword, a different Actabl product, is the one described as powered by 260+ integrations, so read that number carefully during a demo.


## Which platform fits short-term rentals rather than hotels?


Breezeway is the vacation rental answer in this group, built around cleaning and turnover rather than room status. It covers cleaning, inspections with custom checklists, maintenance scheduling and guest messaging, and ships two AI agents: Controller, which produces a daily operations feed with smart task assignment, and Concierge, which answers guests with property context and suggests tasks ([Breezeway](https://www.breezeway.io/) ). It connects to 13 or more systems including Airbnb, Guesty, Cloudbeds, Hostaway, Mews and Hostfully.


Breezeway does not publish pricing. Operators running a mixed portfolio of hotels and rentals tend to end up with Breezeway on the rental side and something else on the hotel side, which is two systems and two sets of reporting.

## What goes wrong when you roll one of these out?


Rollout failure in this category usually traces back to who types the task. A platform that only starts once a supervisor has entered a work order inherits the gaps in the old process, including the 2am request nobody logged and the maintenance issue a guest mentioned in a review instead of a message. Before signing, run one test with each vendor: send a guest message asking for something that needs a decision and a person, then watch how far the system gets before a human touches it. Vendors separate more clearly on that test than on any feature list, so run it before you read the comparison grid.


The second failure is reporting across two systems. Operators who buy a messaging tool and an operations tool separately end up reconciling two task counts that never agree, because one counts guest requests and the other counts work orders.


## FAQ


Common questions about hospitality operations platforms cover what the category includes, which vendors publish pricing, and how these tools differ from guest messaging software. The short answers below each stand on their own, and every figure comes from the vendor's own site.


### What is a hospitality operations platform?


A hospitality operations platform is software that coordinates the work of running a property: housekeeping schedules, maintenance and work orders, guest requests, inspections and inventory. The category overlaps with guest messaging, because a growing share of tasks now start as a guest message rather than a phone call to the front desk.


### Which hospitality operations platform is best for guest tasks and maintenance?


Conduit is the strongest choice when guest requests are the main source of tasks, because the message and the task sit on one agent and its pricing is published at $18 to $48 per unit per month. hotelkit and Flexkeeping are stronger when the work originates inside the building, such as preventive maintenance cycles and complex cleaning patterns.


### Do these platforms publish their pricing?


Conduit publishes package pricing of $18 for Messaging, $30 for Guest, $36 for Guest + Devices and $48 for Full Suite, per unit per month, plus a flat $899 per month Startup plan for 0 to 25 units. hotelkit, Flexkeeping, Quore, ALICE and Breezeway all direct buyers to a demo or sales contact instead of publishing rates.


### Do hospitality operations platforms integrate with a PMS?


Most do, and the specific list matters more than the claim. hotelkit publishes integrations with Mews, Oracle Hospitality (OHIP/OPERA), apaleo and Stay, while Flexkeeping publishes Mews, Cloudbeds, Oracle Opera Cloud, RMS, Apaleo and Shiji. Breezeway publishes 13 or more, including Airbnb, Guesty, Cloudbeds, Hostaway and Mews. Ask whether the integration writes back to the PMS or only reads from it, because a read-only connection leaves staff updating two systems by hand.


### What is the difference between an operations platform and a guest messaging tool?


An operations platform organises work after it has been identified, through task lists, schedules and work orders. A guest messaging tool handles the conversation that often identifies the work. The two categories are converging, and the practical question for a buyer is how many systems a single guest request has to cross before it is finished.


### Which platform suits short-term rentals rather than hotels?


Breezeway is built for short-term rental operations. Its cleaning, turnover and inspection workflows connect to Airbnb, Guesty, Hostaway and Hostfully, which covers most rental stacks. Conduit also serves rental portfolios at the same published per-unit price, so operators running hotels and rentals together can keep one system.


### How long does implementation take?


None of these vendors publishes a standard implementation timeline, so treat any number quoted in a demo as specific to that deal. Ask for the name of a comparable property by portfolio size, and ask how long that customer took to reach steady state rather than go-live.
